text: Checked reify's gating path for a formatting step and came up empty: the tree carries no rustfmt.toml, `hooks/pre-commit` never shells out to `cargo fmt`, and the only lint scripts/verify.sh runs is a clippy pass with `--workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Formatting is simply not enforced anywhere.

To talk to the reify-gui debug MCP you POST JSON-RPC at the `/mcp` suffix of the local server, i.e. `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; aiming at the bare host and port reaches nothing. The binding lives in gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs, written as `.route("/mcp", post(handle_mcp))`.

Documentation and PRD artifacts for reify land as direct commits on main inside the project_root checkout at /home/leo/src/reify. They are deliberately kept out of the orchestrator's merge queue, and scripts/land.sh is not the vehicle for them either.

When a freshly added `crates/<c>/tests/<f>.rs` trips reify's harness-layout gate, let a row count pick the remedy: run `grep -c '^crates/<crate>/' tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` first. A count of zero says the file has to move inside a harness; any count above zero says adding a grandfather row is the sanctioned fix.

`CompiledModule.functions` in reify holds only what the user actually wrote. Compiling through `compile_source_with_stdlib` deliberately leaves every `pub fn` body originating in the stdlib or the prelude out of that map, so it is never a complete inventory of callable functions.

The C1 move for a reify test is `git mv crates/<c>/tests/<f>.rs crates/<c>/tests/harness_<sub>/<f>.rs`, followed by a declaration in `tests/harness_<sub>.rs` reading `#[path = "harness_<sub>/<f>.rs"] mod <f>;`. Dropping the `#[path]` attribute is the trap: a plain `mod <f>;` at an integration-test crate root binds to the sibling `tests/<f>.rs` rather than the file you just moved.

Cargo's freshness test for a build script is a plain mtime comparison, strictly greater and at nanosecond precision: every `cargo:rerun-if-changed` path is measured against `target/<profile>/build/<pkg>-<hash>/output`. No separate timestamp file is involved — that `output` artifact is itself the reference clock.

Read the `files` list on an architect plan as a write-set. It should enumerate only the paths the task will create or edit; anything the task merely reads, imports, calls into, or leaves untouched belongs under `reuse` instead.

Curator gate esc-5564-1 retired the reconciliation misroute finding on 2026-07-27. The assertion that project_id=reify resolves to project_root=/home/leo/src/dark-factory no longer describes live behaviour — the correction is durable in code, so the condition should not be treated as open.

A Rust `tracing` test that installs a capturing subscriber with `tracing::subscriber::with_default` can flake invisibly: that binding is per-thread, while callsite `Interest` is memoized once per process. Let a sibling test in the same binary reach the callsite with no subscriber installed and the Interest freezes at `never`, and the event you assert on is dropped silently.

`MockGeometryKernel::tessellate` in crates/reify-test-support/src/mocks.rs long returned a lone unclosed triangle, which `Mesh::validate` rejects under `MeshInvariant::Closed` — so every consumer of the mock quietly escaped the INV-GEO-1 contract without saying so. Commit ef4187454d closed that hole on 2026-07-26 under task #5105 δ.

`reify-audit --pattern PTODO` refuses to start from a linked worktree. The CLI opens the orchestrator runs.db eagerly at startup, falling back to `data/orchestrator/runs.db`, and since that file is git-untracked it is absent from every worktree, so the process exits 125. That 125 signals a broken setup, never a findings tally.

Harness-tracked background tasks get reaped on this host roughly once an hour, so a Claude session that needs to be woken after a long wait should hang that wake-up on the harness Monitor tool instead of a background-Bash watch loop that may not outlive the reap.

The Graphiti edges 3ef4c09f and 912e58e8 lack source episodes on purpose: those episodes were removed while cleaning up the task-5422 memory fabrication. They are intentional leftovers, not corruption, and deleting them as a "repair" would be wrong.

Faking a nextest-less host for reify's tests/infra/test_verify_*.sh suites decomposes into two separate exercises that answer different questions: making scripts/verify.sh genuinely walk its NEXTEST=0 fallback by hiding cargo-nextest properly, versus sed-ing a throwaway copy of a suite so only the suite's own belief about nextest changes.

An architect re-invoked on a task/NNNN branch can find every TDD commit still present while `.task/plan.json` has gone missing or drifted out of sync. Recovery is to rebuild a plan.json that faithfully mirrors the steps already committed on the branch, rather than discarding and redoing that work.

The reify-gui debug MCP carries a catalogue of gotchas sharing one signature: they answer confidently and wrongly instead of failing, and each has already produced a false conclusion in at least one real session. It reads as the appendix to topic=reify-debug-mcp-driving, which covers ports, transport and launch recipes.

Both `pkill -f` and `pgrep -f` match their pattern against whole command lines, and the shell running your own invocation has that very pattern sitting in its command line. So never select processes to signal with a pattern that your own command contains.

Whether reify's compiler hangs a `GeomRef::Sub` consumption edge on a `Boolean{left,right}` operand turns on the operand's shape and nothing else: cross-sub `self.<sub>.<member>` forms acquire one, while a bare identifier naming a sibling geometry-let, or a function call, does not.

Adding a frontend-mediated tool to the reify-debug MCP costs exactly two edits: a `ToolDef` entry inside `tool_defs()` in gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs, and a matching handler in the `buildHandlers(ctx)` map in gui/src/debug/bridge.ts. The Rust dispatch needs no new match-arm at all.
